source.title: Learning Layer-wise Equivariances Automatically using Gradients
source.citation: T. V. D. van der Ouderaa et al., 2023
source.authors: T. V. D. van der Ouderaa; Alexander Immer; Mark van der Wilk

record.tranche_reason: Compares fully connected, convolutional and learnable symmetry networks on image tasks and reports test performance; this conceptually tests the architecture/generalization part of V3 using a different architecture and training objective.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy and NLL for architecture variants, including a fully connected network and convolutional baselines. Its main symmetry-learning objective also compares these models. It does not test memorization of random labels, width beyond interpolation, optimizer comparisons, batch size, dropout, generalization measures, or memorized-example removal. Table 7 compares convolutional factorisations but is not a fully connected versus convolutional comparison under the stated V3 claim.
record.test_reason: The standard MAP experiments directly compare held-out classification accuracy of fully connected and convolutional networks trained from scratch with Adam, using an architecture adapted from Neyshabur (2020). These test V3; training–test gaps are unnecessary because V3 concerns test error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The method learns layer-wise equivariance through approximate marginal-likelihood optimization, selecting mostly convolutional structure on CIFAR-10 while relaxing symmetry where useful. It selects among supplied symmetry representations rather than discovering arbitrary symmetry groups.
record.recipe_differences: Compares hard-coded convolutional and fully connected architectures, plus a proposed differentiable Laplace method that learns equivariance; reports test performance rather than train-test gaps. CIFAR-10 training uses Adam, data augmentation and 4000 epochs.
record.method_sensitivity: Task symmetry changes the relative performance of FC and CONV: CONV outperforms FC on the translation-invariant digit task but fails on the location-dependent digit-and-quadrant task. Learned layer structure varies by layer; the CIFAR-10 model is convolutional in most layers and fully connected near the end.

fits_no_version.finding: Learnable FC+CONV hybrids attain CIFAR-10 accuracy within one percentage point of CONV under differentiable Laplace training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Marginal-likelihood optimization can select useful layer-wise equivariance in architectures containing convolutional and fully connected paths.

record.problems: Reported comparisons use test accuracy and NLL, not paired training and test errors; therefore they do not quantify the generalization gap. Most CIFAR-10 architecture comparisons use a specialized differentiable Laplace objective or standard MAP and do not test memorization capacity. The toy task deliberately changes the symmetry structure and does not directly test the claim's same-distribution training-to-test behavior.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
The causal contribution of local connectivity, fully connected networks learning sparse local connections, convolutional initialization, and CIFAR-100 or SVHN comparisons.
Adaptive-versus-SGD comparisons and tuning or recovery conditions.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps.
Retraining after removing memorized versus random examples.

missing.what: Separate fixed-architecture differentiable Laplace rows for Table 1: digit-only FC 97.04%, CONV 99.23%; digit-and-quadrant FC 95.46%, CONV 24.50%. Existing rows conflate these with MAP values.
Separate differentiable Laplace CIFAR-10 comparator rows: FC 52.36%, CONV 84.07%, F-FC 53.38%. These values currently appear under incorrect MAP conditions.

Spatially sparsified CIFAR-10 architecture comparisons: with anchor-point priors, MAP S-FC/S-CONV accuracies are 50.21%/82.53% and differentiable Laplace accuracies are 46.18%/81.29%; with lengthscale priors, corresponding accuracies are 49.69%/81.84% and 52.22%/81.20%.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V3. Its strongest direct evidence is the fixed-architecture MAP comparison. The location-dependent toy task qualifies the architecture advantage because its strict output invariance conflicts with the target; it does not establish failure of ordinary CNNs that preserve positional information. Table 7 compares convolutional variants and supplies no FC-versus-CONV test.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.

The study does not isolate local connectivity as the cause of the performance difference, test sparse learned local connections or convolutional initialization, or use the cited MNIST, CIFAR-100 and SVHN settings. Its main CIFAR-10 setup uses standard data augmentation and a specialized equivariance-learning method.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons and the stated tuning or recovery conditions.
Large versus small batch size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.
